name: GA-09
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+17 partisan lean makes this deeply Republican territory
Incumbent Andrew Clyde holds a large fundraising and cash-on-hand edge
Prediction markets price Clyde's win probability near 97%
No public polling or expert ratings indicate a competitive race
model.rationale: The district's R+17 lean, Clyde's incumbency and roughly seven-to-one fundraising advantage, and prediction markets pricing him near 97% all point the same direction, with no polling or expert ratings suggesting competitiveness.
model.watch: A late scandal, a surge of outside spending against Clyde, or unexpected polling showing a single-digit race would be the main signals of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Georgia's 9th District is firmly Republican territory, with a partisan lean of roughly seventeen points toward the GOP. Andrew Clyde, the incumbent, is running for another term after securing renomination. His campaign has raised about $728,000 to Caitlyn Gegen's roughly $98,000, and he holds a wide cash-on-hand advantage heading into the general election. Outside spending on both sides has been modest.

Prediction markets give Clyde about a 97% chance of winning, and no polling or expert ratings treat the race as competitive. The district's strong Republican lean, the incumbency advantage, and the financial gap all align in the same direction. Barring an unexpected late development, Clyde is positioned to win another term by a margin of roughly seventeen points.
